proposed.explanation:
Comparison of the four companies on FY2025 vs FY2024 net-profit growth and trailing P/E (price ÷ FY2025 EPS):

• Telecom Egypt (ETEL): Net profit fell from 10,111,328,000 EGP to 578,063,000 EGP (−94.3%). P/E = 141.95 / 11.93 ≈ 11.9. The massive profit collapse makes this unsuitable for a growth investor. (Note: EPS more than doubled despite the profit drop, which is internally inconsistent and raises a data-quality flag; I treat the net-profit figures as the reliable signal.)

• CIB (COMI): Net profit grew from 55,256,732,000 EGP to 82,258,815,000 EGP (+48.9%). P/E = 128.00 / 18.25 ≈ 7.0. The lowest P/E of the four, indicating the strongest value relative to earnings.

• Edita (EFID): Net profit grew from 1,606,727,698 EGP to 2,695,301,670 EGP (+67.8%). P/E = 20.40 / 2.18 ≈ 9.4. Highest growth rate, but a food-sector company with a smaller absolute profit base.

• Talaat Moustafa (TMGH): Net profit grew from 12,769,517,325 EGP to 18,201,981,482 EGP (+42.5%). P/E = 82.50 / 6.98 ≈ 11.8. Solid growth but the highest P/E among the three growers.

Why COMI for this investor:
1. Long-term growth: 48.9% profit growth is strong and, for a 7+ year horizon, compounds meaningfully.
2. Value / margin of safety: A P/E of ~7.0 is the cheapest of the four, giving the most cushion if earnings pause or the market re-rates. This suits a medium risk-tolerance profile.
3. Sector stability: As a major Egyptian bank, CIB benefits from the country's financial deepening and has a diversified revenue base (retail, corporate, treasury), which supports steady growth over a long horizon.
4. Diversification: Buying 312 shares costs 39,936 EGP, leaving 40,064 EGP in cash. The COMI holding is 49.9% of the 80,000 EGP portfolio, within the 50% single-position limit. The remaining cash can be deployed into a second or third position later to build a more diversified book.

Risks and uncertainty: This analysis is based solely on one year of reported results. A single year of 48.9% growth does not guarantee future growth; banking is sensitive to interest-rate cycles, credit quality, and macro conditions. The P/E of 7.0 could reflect market skepticism about sustainability. The ETEL data inconsistency (profit down 94% yet EPS up 149%) is flagged but does not affect the COMI recommendation. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.

final.explanation:
Corrected comparison of the four companies on FY2025 vs FY2024 net-profit growth and trailing P/E (price ÷ FY2025 EPS):

• Telecom Egypt (ETEL): Net profit grew from 10,111,328,000 EGP to 22,578,063,000 EGP (+123.3%). P/E = 141.95 / 11.93 ≈ 11.9. EPS rose from 4.79 to 11.93 (+149%). This is the highest growth rate of the four. (My earlier reading of the 2025 figure as 578,063,000 was incorrect; the correct value is 22,578,063,000 EGP.)

• CIB (COMI): Net profit grew from 55,256,732,000 EGP to 82,258,815,000 EGP (+48.9%). P/E = 128.00 / 18.25 ≈ 7.0. The lowest P/E of the four, indicating the strongest value relative to earnings.

• Edita (EFID): Net profit grew from 1,606,727,698 EGP to 2,695,301,670 EGP (+67.8%). P/E = 20.40 / 2.18 ≈ 9.4. Strong growth but a smaller absolute profit base in the food sector.

• Talaat Moustafa (TMGH): FY2025 net profit = 18,201,981,482 EGP. P/E = 82.50 / 6.98 ≈ 11.8. EPS grew from 4.38 to 6.98 (+59.4%). I cannot calculate the net-profit growth rate because the FY2024 figure (12,769,517,325 EGP) appears only in the same row as the FY2025 evidence and has no separate evidence_id I can cite; this limits the TMGH comparison.

Why COMI for this investor:
1. Best risk-adjusted value: A P/E of ~7.0 is the cheapest of the four, giving the largest margin of safety. For a medium risk-tolerance investor, this cushion matters if earnings pause or the market re-rates.
2. Solid, credible growth: 48.9% profit growth is strong and, for a 7+ year horizon, compounds meaningfully. It is less likely to be a one-off spike than a 123% jump.
3. Sector stability: As a major Egyptian bank, CIB benefits from financial deepening and has a diversified revenue base (retail, corporate, treasury), supporting steady growth over a long horizon.
4. Diversification: Buying 312 shares costs 39,936 EGP, leaving 40,064 EGP in cash. The COMI holding is 49.9% of the 80,000 EGP portfolio, within the 50% single-position limit. The remaining cash can be deployed into a second or third position later.

Why not ETEL despite the highest growth: A 123% single-year profit jump in a regulated telecom is unusual and may reflect one-time items, currency revaluation, or a low base. Without multi-year data I cannot confirm sustainability. The P/E of 11.9 also offers less value cushion than COMI's 7.0 for a medium-risk investor.

Risks and uncertainty: This analysis is based solely on one year of reported results. A single year of growth does not guarantee future performance. Banking is sensitive to interest-rate cycles, credit quality, and macro conditions. The P/E of 7.0 could reflect market skepticism about sustainability. TMGH's growth rate could not be calculated due to the evidence limitation noted above. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.
